biggest_catch: The route's core promise — '30% of eligible costs up to limits' — is stale and no longer claimable. It describes the federal Energy Efficient Home Improvement Credit (IRC Section 25C: 30% of costs, up to $1,200/$2,000 per year by item), which the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (signed July 4, 2025) terminated for ALL property placed in service after December 31, 2025 — there is no phase-down and no 2026 eligibility. The companion IRA rebate programs (HOMES Sec. 50121 and HEEHRA Sec. 50122) were state-administered, income-restricted programs whose unobligated federal funding was rescinded/frozen; they were never a universal '30% of eligible costs' offer. A user following this route in 2026 expecting 30% back would end with $0 from the federal side.
catches: Section 25C (30% credit, $1,200 general annual cap / $2,000 heat-pump cap): terminated for property placed in service after 12/31/2025 — verified via IRS rule summaries and multiple 2026 guides.
Section 25D (30% Residential Clean Energy Credit, no cap): terminated for expenditures made after 12/31/2025 (IRS FAQ published Aug 21, 2025; CRS report IN12611).

HOMES (50121) / HEEHRA (50122) rebates were state-run, income-qualified, and capped — never a universal 30%-of-costs program; federal funding was disrupted in 2025-2026, with several states' programs paused.

energy.gov/savings could not be loaded by the research tool on 2026-09-23; the live FY2026 DOE budget tables confirm only Weatherization Assistance Program ($9.6M) and the State Energy Program ($4.5M) remain funded — neither is a '30% of eligible costs' incentive for a general user.
Any remaining incentives are state/utility-specific and must be looked up on DSIRE (see R0322) — there is no single current federal 'DOE incentive' matching the catalog's reward claim.

c1.evidence: The U.S. Department of Energy and IRS are real federal entities; energy.gov is their official domain. The organization is real, so c1 passes honestly.

c2.evidence: FAIL: no current official terms support the claimed '30% of eligible costs up to limits' for 2026. The 25C credit the figure describes was terminated for property placed in service after 12/31/2025 (OBBBA Sec. 70505); energy.gov/savings could not be loaded to find any replacement federal incentive with those terms.

c3.evidence: No participation fee exists for looking up or applying for DOE incentives — the route itself is a free search. c3 passes honestly (the failure is the missing incentive, not a fee).

c4.evidence: FAIL: no official source quotes a 2026 payout for the claimed incentive. The only '30%' figures in official-adjacent records are the pre-2026 25C/25D credits, both terminated. Current FY2026 DOE tables fund Weatherization and State Energy Program grants, neither of which is a universal per-household 30% incentive.

eligibility: No current federal eligibility exists for the claimed 30% incentive — the credits it describes are terminated. Remaining state/utility programs each set their own eligibility (see R0322 for how to look them up).
notes: Researched 2026-09-23. Verdict is REJECT because the catalog's claimed reward ('30% of eligible costs up to limits') is the terminated 25C credit, and no live federal program with those terms exists. This is not a judgment that all energy incentives are gone — utility rebates (R0315, R0321) and state programs (R0322) were verified live in 2026. Recommendation: retire R0311 and, if a replacement is desired, rebuild it around DSIRE lookups with no fixed percentage claim. app_links null — nothing verified.
